newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine gross int'l reserves at $12.25 bln.
newsitem.headline: Philippine gross int'l reserves at $12.25 bln.

text.p: Strong investment flows nudged up the Philippines' gross international reserves to a record $12.25 billion as of March 17, the Central Bank said in a statement on Tuesday.
The Central Bank had recently reported the reserves at $12.05 billion at March 5 and $11.7 billion at the end of 1996.

"Given the current state of investor confidence on the Philippines, the targeted end-year gross international reserves level of $14 billion projected by the Central Bank will certainly be achieved within a shorter time frame," Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said.
Since January, the Central Bank said it bought a net of $1.237 billion from banks.
Foreign currency deposits in banks rose to $14.854 billion at the end of February, up $5.11 billion from the year-ago level of $9.74 billion, the Central Bank said.
